newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher for fifth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher for fifth straight day.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Wednesday for the fifth straight day as the star electronics sector continued to attract buying despite market temptation to take profits at current high prices, brokers said.
The index ended up 27.13 points or 0.33 percent at 8,282.91, off an intraday high of 8,316.38.
Turnover was a moderately active T$117.4 billion.
Electronics continued to lead the gains, rising 2.53 percent despite growing expectations of profit-taking after the sector's persistent gains since an April-May correction, brokers said.

"Many had expected electronics to face a downward correction after the recent rally, but both institutional and individual investors simply are afraid of missing the last rallying train," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
Hung said many institutional investors had sold down their electronics holdings and now were laying in more. "They are now forced to cover short positions on electronics."
Leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor rose T$4 to T$128.5 due to the short-squeeze, brokers said. Chipmaker United Microelectronics surged T$3.5 to T$82. Both shares hit new 1997 highs.
Chipmaker Winbond Electronics rose T$1 to T$41.6 after saying it won T$3.03 billion in insurance compensation for an October 1996 fire loss.
Acer Peripherals rose the daily seven percent limit to T$72 as it went bonus issue on Wednesday.
More than half of the market's trading has focused on electronics in recent sessions, brokers said.
Nan Ya Plastics gained 50 cents to T$76 as it went stock dividend issue on Wednesday.
Brokers noted investor caution as the index neared quarterly average resistance at 8,288.
